newsitem.title: JAPAN: Nissan won't comment on Automakers purchase talk.
newsitem.headline: Nissan won't comment on Automakers purchase talk.

text.p: Nissan Motor Co Ltd declined to comment on Friday on speculation in South Africa that it might be about to take stake in or full control of South African firm Automakers Ltd.
Automakers share price rose sharply on Thursday due to the market talk in Johannesburg. Nissan has no stake in Automakers.
"We cannot make any comment because it is related to the stock market," a Nissan spokeswoman said.

Automakers is the holding company of Nissan South Africa (NSA), which has been assembling Nissan-designed Pulsar compact car, the Cefiro luxury sedan and pickup trucks with Nissan's technical assistance since 1983. It produced 42,000 Nissan-designed cars in 1995. NSA also produces Fiat SpA's Uno compact car with a production of about 17,000 a year.

In October last year, Toyota Motor Corp bought a 27.8 percent stake, or 11.3 million shares, in Toyota South Africa Ltd (TSA) for 446 million rand, (10 billion yen), from Johnnies Industrial Corp Ltd (Johnnic). TSA is 50 percent owned by Wesco, an independent South African holding company.
